evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: participants in randomized curcumin supplementation trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of three randomized trials did not find a statistically significant homocysteine-lowering effect of curcumin; the primary analysis was limited to two trials with interpretable values.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; null result with very low certainty
evidence.safety_note: The evidence base was very small, heterogeneity was extreme, and one source dataset contained physiologically implausible values; this is a strong counterweight to a confident homocysteine-lowering claim.

evidence.effect_or_condition: exercise capacity and blood pressure in COPD
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
evidence.population: adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of 12 studies involving 357 people with COPD found a small pooled improvement in exercise capacity and lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure with nitrate-rich beetroot juice.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; disease-specific signal with design-sensitive estimates
evidence.safety_note: Parallel-trial and crossover-trial estimates differed materially, so the pooled result should not be generalized to healthy athletes or treated as a uniform exercise-performance effect.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 synthesis of 23 randomized trials found signals for faster time to peak power and greater handgrip strength, but no clear benefit for short sprint times, mean or peak power, perceived exertion, heart rate, or blood lactate.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; mostly low to very low certainty
evidence.safety_note: Female representation was limited and most pooled outcomes were null; the evidence does not support a broad claim that beetroot juice reliably improves short-distance or repeated-sprint performance.

evidence.effect_or_condition: sleep outcomes in people with cancer
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
evidence.population: people with cancer and sleep-related outcomes
evidence.sample_size: 7 studies pooled; 13 articles in the systematic review
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 cancer-specific review found no statistically significant overall pooled improvement in sleep outcomes with melatonin, despite selected subgroup and short-term signals.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; overall null with very high heterogeneity
evidence.safety_note: Heterogeneity was very high, samples were limited, interventions were short, and outcomes were largely subjective; cancer-specific findings should not be generalized to primary insomnia.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of 63 randomized trials reported small pooled changes in several glycemic, anthropometric, and lipid risk factors with alpha-lipoic acid, while LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, and HDL cholesterol were not significantly changed.
evidence.evidence_grade: large systematic review/meta-analysis; mixed surrogate outcomes
evidence.safety_note: The reported changes are surrogate risk factors rather than cardiovascular-event outcomes, and several clinically relevant endpoints were null.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of human studies
evidence.population: people with schizophrenia receiving antipsychotic treatment
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 review of eight studies found no clear placebo-controlled improvement in overall schizophrenia symptoms, BMI, adverse events, discontinuation, or key metabolic outcomes with adjunctive alpha-lipoic acid.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; small evidence base with predominantly null findings
evidence.safety_note: The evidence was limited by small samples and imprecision; isolated subgroup findings should not be reframed as established psychiatric or metabolic benefit.

evidence.effect_or_condition: PCOS hormonal, metabolic, and reproductive outcomes
evidence.study_type: umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 umbrella review found signals across several hormonal, insulin-resistance, and reproductive outcomes with inositol in PCOS, but none of the assessed evidence was rated high certainty.
evidence.evidence_grade: umbrella review; moderate-to-very-low certainty depending on outcome
evidence.safety_note: Results differed by inositol subtype and comparator, and most evidence was low or very low certainty; myo-inositol, D-chiro-inositol, and combination regimens should not be treated as interchangeable.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 synthesis of 34 randomized trials reported pooled improvements across several glycemic, lipid, blood-pressure, inflammatory, and oxidative-stress biomarkers with taurine.
evidence.safety_note: These are pooled surrogate outcomes across heterogeneous trials and do not establish prevention or treatment of cardiovascular disease; dose-response subgroup findings are not consumer dosing guidance.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: adults with and without type 2 diabetes across randomized CoQ10 trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of 39 randomized trials found small pooled changes in fasting glucose, HbA1c, and fasting insulin with CoQ10, with effects more apparent in diabetes populations.
evidence.safety_note: The review rated the evidence very low certainty, so small biomarker changes should not be presented as established diabetes treatment or prevention.

evidence.effect_or_condition: exercise oxidative-stress, muscle-damage, and performance markers
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled studies
evidence.population: participants in randomized exercise studies of CoQ10 analogs
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 synthesis of 14 randomized studies found lower malondialdehyde and creatine kinase after exercise with CoQ10, while blood lactate and maximal oxygen uptake were not significantly changed.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; biomarker signal with performance nulls
evidence.safety_note: Changes in oxidative-stress or muscle-damage biomarkers do not establish faster recovery or improved exercise performance, and the null VO2max and lactate findings remain first-class.

evidence.study_type: umbrella review and re-analysis of meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: participants represented in CoQ10 glycemic meta-analyses
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 umbrella review found fasting-glucose improvement was the most consistent CoQ10 glycemic signal, while conclusions for HbA1c, HOMA-IR, and insulin varied depending on the analytic scale used.
evidence.safety_note: Method-dependent conclusions are a source-integrity warning: glycemic effects should not be summarized as uniformly positive across endpoints.

evidence.effect_or_condition: cardiometabolic risk factors in prediabetes and type 2 diabetes
evidence.study_type: GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: people with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 review of 20 randomized trials reported pooled improvements in triglycerides, fasting glucose, HbA1c, HOMA-IR, C-reactive protein, and HDL cholesterol with CoQ10, while total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, and malondialdehyde were not significantly changed.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; disease-specific mixed surrogate outcomes
evidence.safety_note: The evidence is specific to prediabetes/type 2 diabetes populations and surrogate risk factors; null blood-pressure and LDL findings should remain visible.
